Resolves #19078

The e2e engine tier runs as three shards instead of two. With two, shard 1 took 220–312 s against the 300 s step ceiling, and it timed out after its tests passed three times in a day, dev's own push run among them. The workflow header's rule is *"A shard nearing it gets a sibling, never a higher ceiling"*, so this adds the sibling. A dispatch stays one shard, so a probe keeps its whole denominator.

Evidence: L3 (this PR's own `pull_request` run, [35804943737](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/35804943737), plus a local `--list` of its selection) → L3 required (AC-1 to AC-3 are hosted-run claims).

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1: three `e2e-engine (n/3)` jobs; a dispatch still runs one | The run shows `e2e-engine (1/3)`, `(2/3)` and `(3/3)`. The dispatch arm of the matrix expression is unchanged (`[1]` / `[1]`). |
| AC-2: every shard under 240 s, and the tallies sum to a two-shard dev run's population | `Run e2e` took **198 s / 159 s / 191 s**. Tallies: 71 passed + 3 skipped, 70 passed, 68 passed, which is **212**. A local `--list` of the run's own 8-path selection at `e61b650545` gives `Total: 212 tests in 40 files`. The old `--shard=1/2` lists 122, the 119 passed + 3 skipped of today's timed-out runs. |
| AC-3: shard 1 alone emits the coverage summary | `Report tier coverage`: `success` on shard 1, `skipped` on shards 2 and 3. |

None.
